strings.text: The first two trip events are on the school's Global Education calendar; the other deadlines come from the 2027 trip pages and are not on the calendar yet. Global trips are for Middle and Upper School students; the GSD events are for Upper School students in the program, who typically begin it in 9th grade. Of the four published 2027 trips, Japan, Iceland and France are for students in grades 9–11 when they register, and Switzerland is for grades 6–8. A nonrefundable deposit is due at registration, and the balance can be paid in full or in two installments. Japan and Iceland take 10 to 16 students, Switzerland 10 to 14 and France 8 to 14, with a waitlist after that. Limited financial aid is available toward one global trip during a student's time at Providence Day.

strings.text: Three sister schools — in Québec City, Southampton and Arequipa — with homestays both ways, plus visiting students on campus and families who host.

strings.text: Since 1992, Country Day has built sister-school partnerships in numerous countries; its current partners are in Canada, Peru and the United Kingdom.
strings.t: 1992 থেকে Country Day বহু দেশে সিস্টার-স্কুল অংশীদারত্ব গড়ে তুলেছে; বর্তমান অংশীদারেরা কানাডা, পেরু ও যুক্তরাজ্যে।

strings.text: The two-week exchanges include homestays, sightseeing and some classes, and sister-school students visit Charlotte during the school year. The Southampton exchange has run since 1991 and the Québec exchange since 2017.

strings.text: Trip financial aid requires a Parents' Financial Statement on file with Admissions, plus the Global Programs Financial Aid Application by the trip's deadline.
